steps.content: [On the Road]

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: You sure this is the way?

The jeep jolts along the road toward <color=#fb9259>Alsa Highlands</color>. The midday sun hangs directly overhead outside the window. Its light feels thin and distant, unable to penetrate the growing gloom that swallows the landscape.

steps.speaker: Milonn
steps.content: Yeah... It matches the map. <size=30>Don't blame me if it's wrong...</size>
Milonn concludes his mumbled excuses and curls inward like a frightened animal.
He'd walked right into the verbal trap, but his total surrender leaves Vester with nothing to confront. Vester can only snort in frustration, the fight draining out of him.
The jeep's interior is hot and close, but the silence that follows is worse.
Ordinarily, you welcome silence—those rare moments when you can set the mask aside and just breathe.

But now, with scrutinizing eyes from the back seat and tension humming between your companions, there is no peace. You find yourself mentally rehearsing your cover story on a loop, each iteration wearing the edges a little thinner.

To distract yourself, you study the jeep's interior. Cracks web the upholstery, and dents of varying depth pock the metal frame. This vehicle has clearly weathered its share of struggles. It isn't hard to guess who it belongs to.
Your focus eventually lands on a small bobblehead hyena fixed to the dashboard. With every jolt of the jeep, it nods along in a clumsy, adorable rhythm.
It's clearly handmade from scrap. On closer look, the plastic shell is fissured with cracks, meticulously held together by layers of tape.
Helga notices your gaze and glances over. Her eyes crinkle into a warm, knowing smile.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Little Vick made that for me. Remember her? Short thing, stuck to me like glue at the last gather-up.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: I remember that kid. What's she up to now?

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Oh, that one's never still. Tinkering with Aurum Secretum under Hypatia's watch these days.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: Hmph. That Fraser girl again... She—
Vester catches Helga's gaze in the rearview mirror and immediately thinks better of it. He cuts off mid-thought, his gaze sliding away—then landing squarely on you.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: So, ${PlayerName}, you come from Fraser with Helga? Or one of the other camps?
You tell them you were born and raised in Fraser's refugee district. Your parents died young, leaving you to survive alone on the streets until a twist of fate led you to Helga.
You invent a farland settlement on the spot, describing its destruction in some long-ago catastrophe. Years of solitary wandering, you claim, ended only when Helga took you in.
You rush through the freshly fabricated tale, but your vague answers do not satisfy Vester. He purses his lips, silently turning your words over as if testing their weight.
What Vester doesn't know—cannot know—is that you have no memories at all. Even if someone asked you to recount the simplest detail of DisCity's past, your mind would offer only a blank wall.
If memory is what makes a person, then maybe you haven't lied to them. Perhaps you really don't qualify as a Disian after all.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Why dig up old graves? That's for us wrinkled cabbages. You young folks got the long road ahead to worry about!
Helga's tone is warm, smiling. She catches your eye in the rearview mirror and gives a quick wink. On the dashboard, the little scrap-built hyena wobbles in cheerful accord...
Thud!
The jeep lurches, throwing you forward before your tailbone crashes back into the seat. Pain lances up your spine. Helga groans under her breath and hauls back on the handbrake.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Sounds like the tire's gone. I'll check it. Keep quiet; last thing we need is the Corruptors' company. We're close to Alsa.
Helga hops out of the jeep. In the rearview mirror, you see Vester's eyes darting. He looks ready to start another argument.

Without hesitating, you roll down the window and lean out. Helga spots you and gives a knowing smile, gesturing you over. You shove the door open and stumble out like a drowning person clawing for air.
The long drive has left your legs shaky, but Helga's steadying grip catches you before you falter.
You fetch the toolbox and set it at her feet. She crouches down, her hands moving with practiced efficiency, but her frown deepens with every second.
Then you hear the sound of the rear window rolling down. You glance up to meet Milonn's anxious face peering out.
...What is it?
He remains silent, his bulging eyes rolling in their sockets as they study you. After a suspended moment, he leans closer. You can almost feel the tremor of his lips hovering just above your head.

steps.speaker: Milonn
steps.content: ...This is bad. A bad sign. The mission... It's not gonna work out.

steps.speaker: Milonn
steps.content: <size=30>Vester said the Speaker... c-can't be trusted...</size>
You stifle a weary sigh, your mind scrambling for a reply. Before you can form a word, a snide voice cuts through the air from the other side of the vehicle.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: <size=30>Now, there's really no need for that...</size>
Vester deliberately raises his voice, ensuring every word carries clearly to you and Helga outside the jeep.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: We've got an expert with us, don't we? Brought all sorts of tricks. I'm sure we'll manage.
A tug at your sleeve. Helga wordlessly hands you something: the nail she just pulled from the tire.
It's long. The surface is clean, dry, with no mud. You run your thumb along the shaft, and your fingers catch on rough wood shavings clinging to the threads near the head.
This nail was planted before you even left.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: Of course, if we all end up dead... well, that'd be on the Speaker's poor judgment, wouldn't it?
Helga straightens up, fixing Vester with an unblinking stare.
[Alsa Highlands] (Add gunfire sound)

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: ...Enough!
She picks off several machine gunners with swift precision before ducking back into the trench. Even under the overcast sky, her aim is nothing short of remarkable.
On the <color=#fb9259>Alsa Highlands</color> front, the deafening thunder of battle finally falls silent, leaving only a lingering haze of gunsmoke.

Ranor tucks his canteen back under his coat, his expression crestfallen. The captain ejects her spent magazine, and only as she shifts to pull a fresh one from her pocket does she notice the look on his face.

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: ...Sorry. I'm fine. Save it.

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: Swat us down, then pretend to be polite? Some people have really perfected that act.

The captain's hands clench around the magazine, her knuckles blanching white. Her jaw is set so tight it aches, a desperate dam holding back the torrent. But in the end, she can't bring herself to let it slide.

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: ...Who are you talking about?

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: I'm talking about the fat-ass senators joking over roast beef right now.

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: Oh, and the bootlickers who think a fancy uniform makes them one of them.
In the trench's sudden quiet, the harsh rasp of the captain's breathing fills the space. Ranor's hand moves, lifting the canteen once more—

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: Fraser gave us a home.

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: A home? Don't forget who put us on the street like dogs in the first place. Same people.

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: We're out here bleeding for them, and for what? A few hot meals? Ptui! We joined to live. Not to die forgotten in this shithole!

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: ...Those were your words. Remember?

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: I didn't know any better back then. I only saw what was in front of me. My next meal. That ignorance... that's what kept us in the gutter. It was no life. We couldn't stay there.
She keeps her head down, working the grip of her gun in careful, repetitive motions. A low murmur escapes her, less a conversation and more a whisper to herself.

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: This is the way. We earned our place. And because we stand here, others get to live better...

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: So, you mean... we deserved all that suffering?

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: You ******* hypocrite! Too ashamed of where you came from? Do you even hear yourself?!

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: Open your eyes! Look at us! Everyone's dead! Is this the better life?!

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: That is exactly why their deaths can't be wasted. They mean something—

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: They mean the senators can stuff their faces a little more!!!

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: <size=45>What have they ever given you?! What have they ever lost for you to kiss their boots like this?!</size>

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: Ha... Right. You climbed the ladder. You got your seat at their table. Congrats.

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: Shut up. Shut up! I order you to be silent!

steps.speaker: Ranor
steps.content: Both of you, stop it! Two o'clock, enemy gunner, dug in!

steps.speaker: Ranor
steps.content: ...Freyna? Why are you standing—? FREYNA, GET DOWN!!!
[On the Road]

Helga stalks around the car and wrenches the rear door open with enough force to nearly tear it from its hinges. Vester, who had been slumped against the window, lurches forward and almost pitches out onto the ground.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Vester. Get out here and say it to my face. If you've got a better plan, let's hear it.
Everything about her body suggests confrontation, but her voice betrays no heat. The question comes out calm, almost curious, as though she truly wants to know.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: Hmph, the problem is you're rushing. The Corruptors up in Alsa won't be cleaned up easy, not even if you go yourself!

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: If it comes to it... we could always move on Fraser. Those *************, pushing us to the brink...

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: You talk a good game, and you're not wrong. I wish it were that simple.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: But while you all bicker in meetings, people are starving. What have any of you done but point fingers?

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: We sent people! But where do we find the hands? The supplies? We're stretched thin!

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Right. Everyone's got their troubles. Heard talk last meeting about cutting a few camps loose. Abandon one, then what? Who's next?

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: That was them, not me! I never suggested—

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: We can't even manage relief, and you're talking war with Fraser?

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: This trade route is our last chance. If it stays closed, every camp in the farlands falls. No exceptions.
Vester says nothing. For a long moment, he seems unable to. Then, haltingly, the words come, his voice unsteady.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: Helga, I've got no problem with you...
His gaze drifts around for a moment before finally settling on you.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: What I don't know is whether your new kid here is worth a damn. Last thing we need is dead weight getting us all killed.
In the distraction of this minor conflict, a thick, cloying presence slithers in, enveloping you all without a sound.
The others dismiss it as mere fog, still locked in their standoff. But you recognize the stench: decay and madness intertwined.
It's <color=#fb9259>Mania</color>!
Watch out! We're surrounded by Corruptors!
The moment your warning leaves your lips, Helga is already moving. She kicks off the ground and vaults onto the roof of the vehicle in one fluid motion.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Battle positions! Now!
The group, at each other's throats moments before, snaps into combat mode. Tavera unleashes a low growl and charges to the front. Vester draws his blade, cursing.
Even Milonn grips his cane, though no one expects him to fight.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
Helga's shots drop the leading Corruptors mid-lunge. Tavera seizes the opening and pushes forward.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Tavera, two on your left! I've got your flank!
They fight in perfect sync—one striking from range, the other in close—their combined assault shredding through Corruptors with lethal efficiency.
In a brief lull, Helga's eyes snap to yours, her words quick and clipped.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Watch Vester. Don't let him near your stuff.
Your nod is sharp with comprehension. Vester is nowhere to be seen, and the distinctive whistle of his blade is silent.
Suspicion drives you to the back of the vehicle. There he is, framed by the open trunk, shoulders tense as he searches for something. You lunge, fingers clamping onto his forearm.
What are you doing?

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: Trying to keep us alive, of course! Isn't this what your precious gear is for?
What's in there isn't for this.
You shove him away with all your strength. Vester stumbles, recovers, and snatches the scimitar leaning against the vehicle.

steps.speaker: Milonn
steps.content: H-help... <size=45>Help!</size> <size=50>HELP ME!</size>
From the other side of the vehicle, Milonn screams in terror. You glance over to see Tavera fighting two Corruptors, completely pinned down.
The cry draws Helga's eye. She spins, slamming a fresh magazine home with muscle memory, but the motion is a heartbeat too slow. A Corruptor is already stooping over Milonn's limp body.
Your eyes dart between Vester and your gear. He stands poised, blade in hand, gaze fixed on you.
He hasn't moved, teeth gritted in impatient fury, but his stance has already shifted, ready to bolt past you toward his companion.
The game is over. You break into a dead sprint toward Milonn. A farland curse hisses behind you—Vester is right there.
The two Corruptors looming over Milonn sense your charge. They freeze, then pivot with a slow, horrifying synchronicity. A guttural moan tears from their throats as they fix on you.
Get back!
You step forward, shielding both Milonn and Vester behind you.
Release the shackles
[Alsa Highlands]
The captain collapses against the sandbag wall. A bullet has torn through her shoulder blade. The chilling thought follows: she may never raise a rifle again.

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: ...Why the hell did you take that bullet for me?!

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: You were going to let me rot here anyway. Sooner or later, what's the difference?! ...I was deserting! Let them shoot me for it! Consider it them doing you the favor of a field execution!

steps.speaker: Ranor
steps.content: Freyna, shut it! Now isn't the time for this...
The captain can only watch as Ranor strips off her coat. Her shirt is soaked through, plastered to her skin with blood. He tears the right sleeve clean away and retrieves the alcohol.
A waste of supplies. She tries to push him off, but her hand merely claws at the air before falling—and finding another hand.
Freyna leans close, muttering words the captain can no longer discern. Nothing kind ever comes from Freyna's lips, but the strength to argue is gone. So is the will.
Why did she do it? Her body moved before her mind could catch up.
A final tide of searing pain and blood loss crashes over her, drowning the world in white noise. She closes her eyes and drifts back to a night in Fraser City.
[Flashback]

She was sitting alone on the low rooftop of a tenement house. Across Fraser City, lights blazed in celebration of a distant victory. Below, a clamorous river of revelers flowed through the streets, their joy a distant murmur.
She was so adrift she didn't notice Freyna sidle up beside her, nor the warm bread pressed into her hand.

It was the touch that broke the spell. Freyna rolled up her sleeve and gently touched her arm. The sharp sting made her gasp, snapping her back. She looked down, startled to find the bread in her hand already missing a bite.

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: You... Where'd you steal this from...?
Freyna went still for a heartbeat, then a wide grin lit up her face.

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: Relax! The bakery lady on East Street gave it to me. Said since it's such a big day, it was a blessing for the troops.

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: Her son's enlisted too. She doesn't know when he'll be back... But with how the war's going, it can't be long, right...?

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: Alright, let me see that wound... ******* hell. That old bastard really laid into you...
That morning, she and Freyna had tried to scavenge food from an inspector's house, only to be spotted by a guard. In a nearby alley, they were cornered.
Given the auspicious day, they'd shown "mercy": twenty lashes, then release. For a refugee district thief, it was a lenient sentence.
Now, the stripes on her arm were still raised and tender. Freyna's fingers hovered, not quite touching the angry skin. In a flash, her own wrist twisted up, capturing Freyna's hand in a firm grip.

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: Let's join the army.

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: The army?! Are you cracked? Don't joke like that. Today was my fault... Well, the alley was too damn long! I'll run faster next time. I won't slow you down again.

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: In the army, we'd have food, clothes... and a real name. It's better than this. Besides, we're already good at—
Freyna snickered.

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: Good at what? Picking pockets? They've got guns out there! We'd come back missing pieces...

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: I heard if we sign up together, they'll put us in the same unit. I'll protect you. We'll make it through.

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: ...Don't believe me? Even that inspector today said I had the makings of a soldier. Said it's a waste, me doing this.
She was so excited that she sprang up, yet her hold on Freyna's hand never faltered. She nearly yanked Freyna up with her.
Even on the battlefield, she would never let go of this hand, would she?

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: They're recruiting at the range next week. They'll give us rifles! Hit the 8-ring with one shot, and we're in.

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: Once I'm in, I'll do something big. And when I do...
With her free hand, she formed a pistol, squinted one eye, and aimed it at the golden palace shimmering in the distance.

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: ...Alright, alright, I believe you! Now sit back down...
She raised her finger slightly, and in the distance, fireworks lit up all of Fraser City.
[Alsa Highlands]
She surfaces to a familiar face—Ranor, his expression tight with worry. She has made it back. But Freyna is gone.
[On the Road]

The Corruptors are violently hurled back the instant they touch the red barrier. From ruined chest cavities, they unleash shrieks of pure agony and fury, thrashing wildly against the energy that holds them at bay.
—Bang! Bang!
Two precise shots cut the screams short. The figures jerk and go limp.
Helga dismounts from the car roof with a heavy thud, interposing herself between you and the Corruptor remains. She meets everyone's gaze, the faint wisp of smoke curling from her barrel.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Everyone still in one piece?
Her gaze sweeps over Vester and Milonn, both shielded behind you, then locks onto you in a long, assessing stare.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: Traitor!!!
Vester makes his move in a sudden burst of motion, but Helga reacts instantly, blocking his path with the hard edge of her rifle's stock and hauling him backward.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: What the hell are you doing?!

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: What... what was that just now?! You pulled something out of thin air!

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: You all saw it, didn't you?! That wasn't any farland trick!
Milonn is a silent, curled shape on the earth, his hands shielding his eyes. Vester, driven by a rising desperation, gives him a sharp kick.

steps.speaker: Tavera
steps.content: ...I saw it too. That red thing. Covered in spikes.
As she speaks, her grip tightens around the spear, its tip now unwavering and leveled directly at you.

steps.speaker: Tavera
steps.content: Who are you?

options: Try to keep up the act

choices.text: Try to keep up the act

steps.content: You step forward slowly, calmly meeting all the hostile gazes fixed on you.
I don't know what you're talking about. This mad man just accused me out of—
Before you can finish, Vester shoves past everyone and bolts to the back of the vehicle. He yanks your gear from the trunk.
A heavy metal crate thuds to the ground. The Bureau's emblem and a line of fine DisCity lettering are stamped plainly on the lid.
There's no turning back now. The secret is laid bare.
I'm actually the Chief of DisCity's Bureau of Crisis Control, specifically in charge of handling Mania incidents.
I came here to—
You don't get to finish. Tavera's knuckles whiten on her spear as she drives it toward you.

steps.speaker: Tavera
steps.content: Disian... Die!
However, a hand—wiry and strong—snaps out and catches the shaft mid-thrust, halting it cold.
The moment Tavera sees whose hand it is, all the strength drains from her grip.

steps.speaker: Tavera
steps.content: Speaker... You knew?

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: Knew? She was the one who planned it!

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: Our scouts saw her. The esteemed Speaker slipped into DisCity alone days ago. Now this brat shows up. It's a setup! She's selling out the farlands!

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: This "Disian brat" just saved your lives.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: Only because he'd have died with us! Hmph, I risked everything to expose this—
steps.female_content: Only because she'd have died with us! Hmph, I risked everything to expose this—

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: You call planting a nail in our tire "risking everything"? Leaving us all as Corruptor bait?
Vester freezes at Helga's words.
Helga's hand emerges from her pocket, clutching a twisted metal nail dusted with black tire shards. She raises it slowly, turning it so all can see.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: This came from our tire. It's a nail from the outpost wall. And you were the only one who could've gotten to it.
Her stare pins Vester, intense enough to feel like a physical brand.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: You think you're clever? To expose your "enemy," you'd get everyone on this truck killed? That's acceptable to you?

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: If this mission fails and another camp starves... whose head will that be on?
Vester is speechless. His breath comes in heavy, ragged gasps that fill the silence. In that charged stillness, you decide to—
This is a conflict among the farlanders themselves. You don't feel it's your place to intervene, so you stand beside Helga in silence, an observer.
This seems like the moment to make your stance clear. You step forward, your voice measured and steady.
I did not come here as an enemy of the farlands. In fact, I'm not here on behalf of DisCity.
I came simply because Helga asked, hoping to help the farlands—

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: What's it to you?! Don't you two stand there playing good cop, bad cop with me!
Vester shoves you aside and storms up to Helga.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: Helga, you always think I'm against you. Well, I am! Because you keep trusting outsiders! First that Fraser girl, now this Disian!

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: Yeah, I sabotaged the tire. I wanted to stop us from reaching Alsa! I won't let some Disian hold our fate! How is that any different from bowing to Fraser?!

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: If I hadn't, how else was I supposed to get through to you?! You're so busy protecting this brat, you wouldn't have heard a word!
He's trembling with fury. His finger jabs at you, then hammers hard against his own chest.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: Helga, I don't care if you look down on me. But how I've stood by our people all these years—you've seen it. Everything I've done... has been for the farlands!

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: You want to know if it was worth it? Fine. I can't speak for anyone else, but my life? Take it, if that's what you want!
Helga holds him in her gaze. When her lips part, it's not words that emerge first, but a long, exhausted sigh.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Vester... do you think that makes you a hero?

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Do you think being in charge gives you the right to decide who lives and who dies?

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: This is all for the farlands!

steps.speaker: Tavera
steps.content: ENOUGH!!!
Tavera's roar leaves the group in stunned silence. Her chest heaves, eyes bloodshot and fixed on Helga. Though the tip of her spear dips slightly, her grip on it is still iron-tight.

steps.speaker: Tavera
steps.content: Speaker, I don't care about the rest. Just answer me one thing. Do you really trust him?
steps.female_content: Speaker, I don't care about the rest. Just answer me one thing. Do you really trust her?

steps.content: Helga turns and gives you a long, meaningful look.
[Alsa Highlands]
The captain rips her arm from Ranor's grip. A hot rush signals the wound giving way, leaving a ruin of blood and torn cloth. She doesn't stop. She staggers on, steps faltering but unceasing.

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: Those gun nests she took out are still empty. That's our gap. I can blow us a path.

steps.speaker: Ranor
steps.content: Don't you see? Their attacks are falling apart too! They can't last much longer. Maybe... maybe if we just hold on...

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: She can't hear you... So drop the act. She was the only one who ever bought it.

From a distance, she watches Freyna go. The way she moves is exactly the same: the same quick, light gait that once carried her to a roof's edge in one fluid jump. Freyna would always land first, then turn, arm outstretched, to pull her up after.

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: Ranor, you know what she told me once?

steps.speaker: Ranor
steps.content: What? To punish you? Whatever it was, she was just angry... When has she ever not thrown herself in front of us?
Freyna's skills, already impressive, have been honed to a razor's edge by years of service. Even now, with over a dozen kilos of explosives on her back, she moves with a predator's lightness.
The captain watches, breath held, as if at any moment Freyna will turn.

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: Yeah. Call her "Captain" once, and she'll walk through fire for you. That's why she's so damn grateful for every scrap Fraser tosses her way. I hate that about her... but I also...

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: I've followed her all these years 'cause she promised to keep me alive. Even if she's forgotten... I haven't.

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: I remember... I remember all of it...

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: All I ever wanted... was for everyone to make it out alive...
Is it her wounds? The exhaustion? No matter how hard she drives her body forward, Freyna pulls farther ahead. How can this open path feel endless, longer than that shadowed alley ever did?

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: When she wakes up, tell her. I'm not doing this for Fraser... I'm not noble like her.
Freyna is too skilled, too fast.
She has already gained the high ground. In the next heartbeat, a bloom of red erupts on her chest. Her form twists, a marionette with its strings cut.

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: I'm just a thief... a deserter. And now... I'm going to use that noble duty of hers one last time...

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: Live for me. After all... it doesn't matter who survives. It's all the same.

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: Stop... Stop! That's an order...!

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: FREYNA!!!
Freyna turns. In the final instant before she falls, her lips part—
Then, the deafening roar. Her body, her unspoken words, everything dissolves in the blast. Ash drifts down like the fading embers of spent fireworks.
[On the Road]

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: I do.
Tavera stumbles back and jams her spear into the mud. She sags against the shaft—the only thing holding her upright.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Not only do I trust this person, I wish every soul in the farlands could do the same, too.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Because this "Disian brat" just saved your lives. And the "Fraser girl" you were talking about is out there digging for Hypercubes for us right now.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: I don't give a damn about factions or borders! The only ones I trust are those who stand on the front line!

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: And you... you think as long as you say it's "for the farlands," it doesn't matter if everyone on this truck dies? If more people starve?

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Fine. You want to be honorable—I won't argue. But don't you dare call what you're doing "for the farlands" ever again!
No one answers. Her words hang in the air, thick and unclaimed, before sinking into an absolute silence.

steps.speaker: Tavera
steps.content: I see. If that's what you believe...
Her jaw tightens, every muscle straining as if to physically wring the next words from her throat.

steps.speaker: Tavera
steps.content: Forgive me. But I cannot follow you, Speaker.

steps.speaker: Tavera
steps.content: The Disians slaughtered my people. How can you ask me to just... forget all those lives?
She retreats slowly, arms folded tight across her chest, her gaze fixed firmly elsewhere. Vester releases a quiet breath of relief and nods to Tavera, an unspoken approval.

steps.speaker: Tavera
steps.content: Don't look at me like that. You're a traitor too.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Yeah... So many lives lost. How could anyone forget?
Helga lowers her gaze and nods wearily.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Fine. If that's your choice, I won't force you.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Whether you want to survive, or stay true to your roots... you're not wrong. None of you are.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: I won't order anyone to walk a path they don't believe in.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: But me? I'm not stopping. This road has to be opened, no matter what.
A heavy silence descends, broken only by the wind's low, mournful whistle.
Into that quiet, you move to stand beside Helga. Without speaking, you bend down, lift the equipment from the ground, and settle its weight onto your shoulder.
Let's go.
Something shifts in Helga's eyes. The faintest smile touches her lips, and she gives you a single, solid nod.
You and Helga unload the gear and explosives from the jeep. No one offers to help. No one says goodbye.
But the road ahead is treacherous for everyone. After a moment, you retrieve two spare Bureau-issue weapons from your pack and approach the three staying behind.
Take these. They're shock devices designed to deal with Corruptors. More effective than regular bullets.
Vester scoffs and turns his head away. Tavera hesitates, then squeezes her eyes shut.
Only Milonn accepts, his hands trembling as he cradles the devices. He stares at their cold metallic gleam, handling them as though they held the weight of his survival.
You walk over to Helga. She is gazing out at the wasteland, her expression distant.
For... the farlands?
She gives a slow nod, then shakes her head, as if arguing with herself. Her boots scrape heavily against the ground.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Doesn't matter who it's for. I want to carve out a path that keeps people alive.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: ${PlayerName}, tell me... Do you think this path can work?
It will. We haven't given up yet, have we?
...I don't know. But I know if we don't start walking now, it never will.

Helga listens in silence. She offers no words, only raises her hand and rests it firmly on your shoulder. You feel the weight of it—steadying, grounding—and beneath that certainty, the faintest tremor.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Let's go.
You cast one last look behind you. The jeep stands motionless where you left it, the three silent passengers blurred into silhouettes by the thick air.
Mm.
<color=#fb9259>Alsa Highlands</color> waits just beyond.
[Alsa Highlands - Convergence]

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: Almost there...
Ranor clutches his rifle to his chest, leaning against the bunker wall, his breaths shallow and frayed.
<color=#fb9259>Alsa Highlands</color> lies in unnatural silence. Yet, the captain hears whispers—the wind, or the dead?
The 24th Company began with twenty-eight. Now, only two remain.
Before them stretches the path Freyna blasted open, a scar leading forward and upward. It seems impossible that someone so slight could have carved such a wide road.
At the thought, her body sways.

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: Ranor, let's go.
Ranor gives her a weak smile.

steps.speaker: Ranor
steps.content: Okay... let's go. We're... we're going home...
He braces on his hands, tries to rise, sways, then crumples to his knees before her. His rifle clatters. Blood pours from his chest.

The captain retrieves the pocket watch from the wound. His father's gift. His "lucky" charm, though luck had abandoned his father years ago to a sickbed. Just moments before, Ranor had said the watch stopped a bullet for him.
It did. Just not enough. The cheap metal casing was no match for the round.
Ranor is now still. She closes her fingers around the watch. Its tiny heart has ceased to beat.
The battlefield falls into a silence so profound, one could almost call it—
<color=#fb9259>Peaceful.</color>
The thought is an intrusion. A sob claws at her throat. She cannot draw a full breath.
Soaked in blood and filth, she squeezes her eyes shut, then opens them. She straightens her broken posture, lifts her chin, and takes a step. Then another.
Above, dark silhouettes sway into view.
Reinforcements? They've... finally come.
Fraser's promise... it was real. They only had to hold on a little longer.
For the first time, she lowers her weapon and raises her hands. Forgotten sunlight washes over her face. Her shoulder pulses, a flare of pain with every step.
Yet it is this very pain that reminds her she is still alive. It nearly brings her to tears.

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: This is... Fraser Army, 24th Company. Sole survivor reporting. Captain—

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Helga.</color>
[Shift Perspective]
The Alsa Highlands unfold before you. Unthinking, you've drifted to the cliff's edge. The wind sweeps past, carrying dust into the void.
The view is brutally clear: below the highlands, there is only a churning sea of shadows and bleached bones—a mass grave where friend and foe are long since indistinguishable.
Helga crouches slowly beside you. She scoops up a handful of dry earth, then opens her fingers, letting the sand and grit trickle back down. It falls like a quiet, gritty defiance.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: I really thought they were coming to save us. What a damn joke... I led everyone around me to their deaths with my own hands, and here I am, still breathing.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: The shadows I saw... they were soldiers already lost to Mania. No sense left in them. If there had been, Freyna wouldn't have made it over the ridge at all.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: In the end... even our enemies had written us off.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: This is... our story.
